[QUERY] Do you ever have monthly abdominal or pelvic cramping/ pain that comes and goes in a cycle (like monthly), even though you don't have bleeding?

[REFERENCE] N/A
[RESPONSE] I'm not sure — I don't recall having monthly abdominal or pelvic cramping that comes and goes in a cycle.

[QUERY] Do you have increased facial or body hair (like a mustache, beard, or thick hair on the chest/abdomen/thighs) or troublesome acne? If yes, when did it start?

[RESPONSE] I have a history of severe acne. I was also noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth.

[THOUGHT] The history of ambiguous genitalia at birth (clitoromegaly, labial fusion) plus severe acne and primary amenorrhea strongly suggests prenatal/ongoing androgen excess — most likely 21-hydroxylase congenital adrenal hyperplasia (classic or nonclassic). The single most specific, high-yield test to support 21-hydroxylase deficiency is a serum 17-hydroxyprogesterone (17-OHP) measured in the morning; an elevated basal 17-OHP (or an exaggerated rise with ACTH stimulation) would confirm the diagnosis. I will request that test next.

[THOUGHT] A normal 17-OHP makes classic 21-hydroxylase CAH less likely despite neonatal virilization. To distinguish an adrenal source of excess androgens (adrenal CAH or adrenal tumor) from an ovarian source, a single high-yield test is a morning serum DHEA-S (primarily adrenal). I will request that lab next.

[TEST] Order a morning (8 AM) serum DHEA-S level (include units and reference range).

[THOUGHT] The combination of neonatal virilization, absent breast development, tall stature, ovarian cysts, and normal adrenal steroid markers strongly suggests aromatase (CYP19A1) deficiency. A classic historical clue is maternal virilization during the pregnancy from which the patient was born because placental aromatase normally protects the fetus and mother; absence of that causes maternal virilization. Confirming that history would meaningfully increase diagnostic probability before ordering hormone/genetic tests.

[QUERY] Did your mother have signs of virilization (excess hair growth, deepening of voice, increased acne, or clitoromegaly) while she was pregnant with you?

[REFERENCE] 4. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin.

[RESPONSE] Yes — my mother reports she had abnormal hair growth on her chin while pregnant with me.

[THOUGHT] The patient is a 16-year-old genetically female with primary amenorrhea, absent breast development (Tanner I), neonatal virilization (clitoromegaly, labial fusion), severe acne, tall stature, multicystic ovaries with a normal uterus, normal adrenal steroid markers (17-OHP and DHEA-S), and a history of maternal virilization during pregnancy. These findings point to inability to aromatize androgens to estrogens: excess fetal/adult androgens cause virilization and cystic ovaries while lack of estrogen prevents breast development and causes continued linear growth. Normal adrenal tests make adrenal CAH or adrenal tumor unlikely. The single most likely diagnosis is aromatase (CYP19A1) deficiency.

[DIAGNOSIS] Aromatase (CYP19A1) deficiency.
